subject.title: [Feature]: Improve OpenClaw upgrade experience when Node.js version requirement changes

question: Should `openclaw update` manage Node versions owned by tools such as nvm, or stop after compatibility preflight and launch a supported installer-driven migration flow?
rationale: Current main safely detects incompatible service runtimes but deliberately does not own arbitrary version-manager state, so the permanent automation boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Guided installer handoff
options.body: Preserve the active installation and launch a supported migration flow that installs a compatible Node, stages OpenClaw, repairs state, rebinds the service, and verifies readiness.

options.title: Manage version managers directly
options.body: Teach the updater to install and select Node through supported version managers, accepting broader shell, platform, and package-scope ownership.

options.title: Improve preflight only
options.body: Retain the current fail-safe boundary but provide exact installer and repair commands with clearer diagnostics rather than migrating Node automatically.

recommendation.title: Guided installer handoff
recommendation.body: Preserve the active installation and launch a supported migration flow that installs a compatible Node, stages OpenClaw, repairs state, rebinds the service, and verifies readiness.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history shows this person reviewing and closing the related update/install-boundary work, making them the strongest product-direction routing candidate.
